Childcare Vouchers
Use of Childcare Vouchers
College Town Primary School accept childcare vouchers but only for specified activities within the rules of the Government Childcare Voucher Scheme.
Childcare vouchers are only acceptable for the following eligible activities:
Childcare vouchers are not accepted for the following:
Please be aware that, under HMRC rules, any overpayment of childcare vouchers cannot be refunded directly to parents due to the tax benefits received on purchase.
College Town Primary School is set up with a number of different childcare voucher agencies including; Edenred, Care-4, Sodexho, Gemelli, ComputerShare and Bravo Benefits. Other providers can be set if required. You need to register for these schemes through your workplace.
The school’s Edenred school number is P20537813.
The school's Sodexo provider ID is 823128.
The school’s Gemelli carer no. is C05963
The school’s Computer Share carer no. is 0023289433
We are also set up with the Government's tax free childcare scheme, to register for this you need to do so through their portal and select College Town Primary School as your childcare provider. More information can be found here: https://www.gov.uk/help-with-childcare-costs/tax-free-childcare
For further queries please email the school at secretary@collegetownprimary.com

pageCache.pageTitle: College Town Primary School - PE and Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
PE and Sports Grant Spend and Impact
The PE Grant (Primary PE and Sport Premium) impacts schools by providing funding to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sport provision for all children, leading to increased pupil engagement, improved teaching skills, a wider range of sports, increased participation in competitive sport, and a greater emphasis on lifelong healthy lifestyles.
Schools are accountable for how they use the PE and Sport Premium funding allocated to them. The Leadership Team at College Town ensures that the funding is spent for the purpose it has been provided: to make additional and sustainable improvements to the PE, sport and physical activity offered.
As part of their role, our governors monitor how the funding is being spent and determine how it fits into school improvement plans and assess the impact it is having on pupils.

Nursery
Caterpillar Class
Welcome to the Caterpillar Class page.
Welcome to Nursery! We are so excited to welcome all of our new children and families. This half-term our topic is All About Me, where we will be getting to know one another, celebrating what makes us unique and building new friendships. Throughout the half-term children will be enjoying painting self-portraits, creating special family books to share the people who are important to them and talking about their home lives through stories, photographs and discussions. We can't wait to begin this exciting learning journey together and make lots of happy memories!
Please could you ensure that your children bring the following named items each day to nursery:

pageCache.pageTitle: College Town Primary School - Wrap Around Childcare
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Childcare
Wake Up Club runs every morning from 7.45am until school starts.
The club is run and managed directly by the school.
Children have the opportunity to play games, draw, colour in and build using construction items such as Lego.
Wake up costs £2.75 per child, per session. Payment is made when booking online via School Gateway.
Please contact the school office if you would like to pay using childcare vouchers.
Afterschool Club runs every day from when school finishes until 6pm.
The club is run and managed directly by the school.
Different activities are planned for the children to enjoy.
The Afterschool club costs £12.50 per child, per session, a light snack is included.
Payment is made when booking online via School Gateway.
Please contact the school office if you would like to pay using childcare vouchers.

SEND
Our vision is: To create and nurture a learning community built upon trust and respect which is fully inclusive and has a passion for lifelong learning. To experience a sense of belonging and well-being for all members of our community; where cooperation and fun go hand-in-hand. To recognise that challenge is the motivator that helps everyone to aspire to excellence in all we say and do.
